name: Question 1
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14197370/assets/4408d1fcee1d168c6ab21ea53cf24845093bad9cc608299a36f0510c1636cc03.png)

Let $D$ be the region enclosed by the curve $C$ parametrized as
$r(t)=⟨{e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡t},\,{e}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}⟩$ for $t\in [0,2\pi ].$ The area of $D$ can be written as

$$
\text{Area}(D)={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})dA={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\boxed{}\,dt,
$$

where $P(x,y)=0$ and $Q(x,y)=x.$ Determine the missing part of the equation.
worked_solution:
Our simple, smooth, closed path $C$ is positively oriented, and  

$$
\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y}=1-0=1.
$$

So, according to Green's theorem, we can write the area of the region $D$ enclosed by the curve $C$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(D) & ={∬}_{D}\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∮}_{C}P\,\text{d}x+Q\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

  

Substituting $P(x,y)=0$ and $Q(x,y)=x,$ we get

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,\text{d}x+Q\,\text{d}y={∮}_{C}x\,\text{d}y.
$$

 

The derivative of $r(t)$ is

$$
{r}^{′}(t)=⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,{e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡t},\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,{e}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}⟩.
$$

Therefore, we can write our line integral as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}x\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡t\,{e}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,{e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t}\,dt.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1

Let D be the region enclosed by the curve C parametrized as r(t)=⟨ecos⁡t,esin⁡t⟩ for t∈[0,2π]. The area of D can be written as

Area(D)=∬D(∂Q∂x−∂P∂y)dA=∫02πAAAAAAAdt,

where P(x,y)=0 and Q(x,y)=x. Determine the missing part of the equation.

a
cos⁡tecos⁡t+sin⁡t
b
cos⁡tecos⁡t
c
−sin⁡tesin⁡t
d
sin⁡tecos⁡t
e
−sin⁡tecos⁡t+sin⁡t
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Our simple, smooth, closed path C is positively oriented, and

∂Q∂x−∂P∂y=1−0=1.

So, according to Green's theorem, we can write the area of the region D enclosed by the curve C as follows:

Area(D)=∬DdA=∬D(∂Q∂x−∂P∂y)dA=∮CPdx+Qdy

Substituting P(x,y)=0 and Q(x,y)=x, we get

∮CPdx+Qdy=∮Cxdy.

The derivative of r(t) is r′(t)=⟨−sin⁡tecos⁡t,cos⁡tesin⁡t⟩.

Therefore, we can write our line integral as

∮Cxdy=∫02πecos⁡t⋅cos⁡tesin⁡tdt=∫02πcos⁡tecos⁡t+sin⁡tdt.
